chunks: O you who believe, on you rests (the responsibility) for your own selves. If you follow the right path those who have gone astray will not be able to do you harm. To God have all of you to return, when He will tell you what you were doing.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about individual responsibility and how one's faith affects others?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to clarify the principle of individual accountability (mas'uliyyah) while distinguishing it from the concept of intercession, affirming that one's spiritual state does not automatically transfer to others. It underscores the ultimate return to Allah, where He will reveal the true nature of hidden deeds, a theme resonating with the Shia emphasis on inner sincerity (ikhlas) alongside outward action. The phrase 'to Allah is your return' serves as a reminder of divine omniscience regarding both public and private conduct.
